newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA HELPS LIVELY HELSINKI AHEAD; HARTWALL SOARS.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA HELPS LIVELY HELSINKI AHEAD; HARTWALL SOARS.

text.p: Shares ended lively trade
higher for a third straight day on Thursday, buoyed by early
gains in Nokia on Wall Street and sharp gains in insurers amid
talk of a shake-up in the Finnish sector, brokers said.
Bulls held the ground for most of the session, but at the
close the picture was clouded by early losses in New York.
"We could advance somewhat on Friday if (Finnish) bonds and
Nokia can hold their upward trend," one broker said.
Nokia closed fair trade 3.50 markka up at 202.50.
Hartwall advanced sharply after a positive surprise in its
January-August profits -- up 230 percent.
Hartwall ended lively trade up 11.00 markka or almost nine
percent at 134.00, and brokers still saw scope for more gains.
Insurers Pohjola and Sampo advanced in active trade as
speculation spread that Merita bank, which has major holdings in
both companies, might be looking to sell -- possibly to another
Nordic financial services company.
Pohjola's B share ended at 91.10 markka, up 2.10, after
touching a two-year high of 94.00. Sampo held gains to closed at
a two-year high of 322.00 markka, up 3.00.
The speculation took Merita up 0.13 markka to 9.89 amid
hopes it would boost its returns by selling the assets.
Forestries remained under heavy pressure following
Metsa-Serla's earnings warning on Tuesday.
"There was massive selling, particularly in Metsa-Serla, by
foreign investors," one broker said.
Metsa-Serla's B share lost 0.80 markka at 30.00.
But UPM managed to end up 0.50 markka at 96.50 in brisk
trade, with investors bargain-hunting after recent losses.
Crane maker Konecranes added 4.00 markka to 127.00 in fair
trade on healthy eight-month profits. Shipping company Finnlines
rose 0.80 markka to 97.90 ahead of eight-month results due on
Friday. -- Ilkka Virtanen, Helsinki newsroom +358-0-68050248
